description: We are a three-member team from Dhaka. We are interested in using NASA data and technology to solve real-world problems. Our project, Delta Sentinels, focuses on flood resilience in Bangladesh. It uses satellite flood data and network analysis to identify when villages may become isolated and when emergency aid should arrive.
summary: SafeWindow answers a question every flood responder faces: when does a village lose its last road to a flood shelter, and how long can it hold out? It turns Sentinel-1 radar flood maps into a date-based isolation timeline for every village. Roads from OpenStreetMap that lie under water are cut, and a network analysis checks which villages can still reach a shelter. NASA-ISRO NISAR L-band radar checks our flood maps independently (it sees 94.7-97.8% of our flood as water), follows the 2026 monsoon in HH and HV, and shows water under crops that C-band radar misses. NASA GPM IMERG rainfall, NASADEM and OPERA DSWx-S1 support the analysis. The method was built on the 2022 Sunamganj flood in Bangladesh and tested, with no thresholds changed, on the 2024 flood and on the 2025 Trimmu flood in Pakistan. Both Sunamganj floods isolated the same five villages, home to about 187,800 people. Results reach people through an installable, offline mobile app in Bangla and English with approved village alerts, an admin panel and a rescue platform. SafeWindow is a research prototype, not an official warning system.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

SafeWindow tells flood responders when a village loses its last road to a flood shelter, and how long it can hold out. For each village it answers three questions: when is it cut off from every shelter (a date range between radar passes), when was its road last seen passable and which route to a shelter was possible then, and when may household supplies run out (an estimate).

HOW IT WORKS

1. Flood maps: Sentinel-1 radar images are turned into water maps with an automatic (Otsu) threshold; a NASADEM slope mask removes steep ground.

2. Road cuts: OpenStreetMap roads under water are cut, and a network analysis (networkx) checks which villages can still reach a shelter.

3. Independent check with NASA-ISRO NISAR: L-band GCOV data (HH and HV) from NASA Earthdata / ASF DAAC sees 94.7-97.8% of our flood as water, from a different satellite and radar band. It follows the 2026 monsoon over 21 NISAR dates, including NASA's newest validated product (NISAR_L2_GCOV_V1) up to 9 November 2026, and shows water under crops that C-band misses.

4. Rain and context: NASA GPM IMERG for rain-to-flood lag and a hindcast; NASA OPERA DSWx-S1 for a confidence comparison.

RESULTS

Built on the 2022 Sunamganj flood (Bangladesh) and tested with no thresholds changed on the 2024 flood (unseen year) and the 2025 Trimmu flood (Pakistan, unseen country). Against independent satellites the flood maps agree with IoU 0.81-0.84 (RCM-1, Chaohu-1) in 2022 and 0.74 (SAOCOM) in 2024. Both Sunamganj floods isolated the same five villages (about 187,800 people). In Sunamganj, road cuts match all 3 dated news reports. Results are weaker at Trimmu, and we report that openly. A Nepal flood (Bara-Parsa 2017) runs as a demonstration.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Instead of a flood extent map, responders get a village-by-village timeline: who is cut off, since when, and which roads are a village's only link. Planning analyses show where relief stock could wait before a flood, and rank 71,711 mapped buildings for field checks.

WHAT WE BUILT

- A Python science pipeline (Google Earth Engine, earthaccess, rasterio, networkx), with 305 automated tests.

- A mobile app (React, Vite, Leaflet, Firebase Hosting): installable, works offline, Bangla and English, flood replay, NISAR swipe comparison, village alerts.

- An admin panel where every alert is drafted, checked, approved and logged; a rescue platform for citizens, NGOs and government with server-side privacy rules.

- An automated watch and a daily check on GitHub Actions.

WHAT MAKES IT CREATIVE

It turns radar pixels into a question people can act on (is my village cut off?), and uses two radar bands, C-band and L-band, to check each other.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

No tuning on test data; honest limitations; Bangla-first design for people in flood areas; offline use with weak internet; no alert is sent without human approval. SafeWindow is a research prototype, not an official warning system.
